paragraphs: I'm applying for the Investment Banking Analyst role in the LMG group in New York. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. I'm interested in this seat because it sits close to the client work, with valuation materials and financial research feeding directly into pitches and advice.

My strongest preparation is in valuation, and it comes from MBA coursework rather than live deals. I valued J.M. Smucker using equity and enterprise value bridges and trading comps, built a DCF with WACC, terminal value and sensitivity analysis that I matched against a sell-side model, and built an LBO for the company. At Lenovo I built forecasts and scenario analyses that improved capital efficiency by 15%. At JPMorgan Asset Management I worked on marketing-channel budget allocation, building models to evaluate $10M in spend.

That maps to the models, valuation materials and research an analyst produces here. I know the transaction side would be new for me, and I'm ready to learn it quickly and do the detailed work well. I'd welcome the chance to talk.

outreach: Hi [Name], I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and I'm applying for the Investment Banking Analyst role in LMG. My background is in forecasting and modeling at Lenovo and JPMorgan Asset Management, and in my MBA I built a DCF and LBO on J.M. Smucker and matched the DCF against a sell-side model. I'd love to hear what the team looks for. Would you have 15 minutes for a quick chat?
